description: NOVA MIND integra conocimientos de administración, gestión empresarial e ingeniería bioquímica. Nos interesan la inteligencia artificial, la innovación tecnológica, la ciencia, la sostenibilidad y la solución de problemas. Contamos con habilidades en pensamiento crítico, análisis, planeación estratégica, toma de decisiones, gestión de proyectos, herramientas digitales y trabajo colaborativo. Buscamos transformar ideas en soluciones innovadoras con impacto positivo en nuestro planeta.
summary: We developed "The Museum of Silence," an illustrated 12-page digital comic embedded in an interactive web platform that tells the story of the artifacts left on the Moon by the Apollo 11 mission in July 1969. We addressed the challenge by translating dense NASA technical records into an engaging, accessible visual narrative designed for all audiences—especially children and young space enthusiasts—allowing readers to explore page by page the history behind the Eagle lander, seismometers, laser retroreflectors, goodwill mementos from 73 nations, and everyday tools left behind in the Sea of Tranquility. This project is important because it preserves the historical and scientific memory of these off-world artifacts, reframing perceived "space debris" as a silent museum of human ingenuity that inspires future generations to connect with space science and our lasting legacy in the cosmos.
details:
What is it and how does it work? The project consists of a 12-page digital comic integrated into an interactive web platform ("The Museum of Silence"). It visually narrates the story of the objects, scientific instruments, and mementos left on the Moon by the Apollo 11 mission in July 1969. It functions as a digital viewer—accessible via any web browser—that allows users to progress sequentially through scenes of the moon landing and the legacy left behind in the Sea of ​​Tranquility.
Benefits and intended impact? The goal is to transform complex technical and historical data from NASA into a narrative accessible to a general audience—especially young people and children—thereby democratizing scientific outreach. The intended impact is to inspire an interest in scientific careers, foster curiosity about space, and bring new appreciation to the technological heritage left behind in the cosmos.
Tools, languages, and software? The web development utilized HTML and JavaScript to create an interactive interface and fluid navigation; the code was written in Visual Studio Code on a personal computer. Additionally, graphic design and digital illustration software were used to create the pages of the comic.
Creativity and key considerations? The project demonstrates creativity by employing graphic storytelling and an anthropomorphic, reflective perspective toward inanimate objects (such as seismometers, laser reflectors, and everyday tools). Considerations included universal accessibility, responsive design for mobile devices, and the rigorous use of NASA’s open archives and data to ensure the historical accuracy of every element.
